1	# Derivable ChainOperation: implementation contract
2	
3	Status: proposed implementation plan, 2026-09-16. Reviewed against
4	`ddf40bc2eb5fac8f7973b112eb383256cd8aac74`. No runtime change or deployment is
5	performed by this document. It supersedes the ordering in the exploratory
6	[research](../research/2026-09-16-blob-efficiency/README.md).
7	
8	## 1. Objective and fixed scope
9	
10	Fit substantially more ordinary L2 history in one permitted blob transaction by
11	publishing execution inputs rather than complete ordinary blocks. Empty ordinary
12	blocks must not contribute a header-sized DA cost. Follower execution must produce
13	the original blocks and match the commitment actually applied on L1.
14	
15	Only `ChainOperation.operations` changes on the DA wire. Preserve:
16	
17	- The standardized outer message version, semantic messages, signed cross-chain
18	  transaction bytes, call/result/rollback data, and message order.
19	- The terminal Sync block's existing encoding and all `l2_entries` and
20	  `outbound_group_sizes` encodings, values, and order.
21	- Physical blob packing, KZG and public-input binding, contract ABI/storage,
22	  ECDSA/proof-system semantics and cross-chain scheduling/ownership rules.
23	- Existing historical payload decoding and independent follower validation.
24	
25	No zlib, Brotli, or other general-purpose compression. No cross-chain deduplication,
26	new calldata carrier, shared blob channel, hash truncation, or omitted system
27	transaction is part of this change. Internal proving RPC extensions and signer
28	limits are in scope because long spans must be usable at settlement time.
29	
30	## 2. Decisions
31	
32	| Decision | Specification |
33	|---|---|
34	| New inner payload tag | `0x03`, named `TAG_DERIVABLE_ORDINARY`. Existing tags `0x00..0x02` retain their exact meanings. Research-only hypothetical tags were never production assignments. |
35	| First profile | `profile_id = 1`: derive supported post-Merge ordinary Ethereum blocks using explicit common execution inputs; retain full-block exceptions. |
36	| Terminal treatment | Always exactly one full terminal block, with the old integer-list encoding intact. Never apply ordinary omission rules to it. |
37	| Ordinary representation | Total count, common environment, sparse records for nonempty/exception blocks; gaps mean empty blocks executed under that environment. |
38	| Format block ceiling | 65,536 total blocks, including the terminal. Thus at most 65,535 ordinary blocks per v3 payload. This is a format safety bound. |
39	| Signer block default | Change `EEZ_PROOF_SIGNER_MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS` from 512 to **65,536**. Explicit lower operator values remain effective for local admission. |
40	| Other signer quotas | Keep current bounded byte/item/time defaults, detailed in §7. Do not multiply all quotas by the block-count increase. Incremental validation and cached references handle long ordinary history. |
41	| Long-span validation | Prepare and validate ordinary blocks ahead of settlement; reference immutable signer-local validated facts at final proving. Terminal validation remains fresh. |
42	| Activation | Coordinated timestamp-gated v3 reader/writer support, with legacy payload acceptance retained. No fixed calendar date is selected by the implementation. |
43	
44	65,536 blocks span about 36 h 24 min at two seconds per block. This is an admission
45	ceiling, not a claim that 36 hours of arbitrary transactions fits DA, memory or
46	execution budgets. The supported workload envelope is established by §11.
47	
48	## 3. Exact v3 data shape
49	
50	Use canonical Ethereum RLP and explicitly typed Rust `Bytes` for new opaque byte
51	strings. Do not rely on `Vec<u8>` to encode a byte string. Preserve the legacy
52	types for the three unchanged terminal/cross-chain fields.
53	
54	```text
55	0x03 || rlp([
56	  profile_id,                 # integer, exactly 1
57	  ordinary_block_count,       # integer, 0..65535
58	  common_environment,        # fixed-arity list below
59	  ordinary_records,          # ordered list below
60	  terminal_block_legacy,     # old Vec<u8> integer-list item, exact original bytes
61	  l2_entries_legacy,          # old Vec<Vec<u8>> representation, unchanged
62	  outbound_group_sizes       # old Vec<u16> representation, unchanged
63	])
64	
65	common_environment := [
66	  timestamp_step_seconds,     # nonzero u64
67	  fee_recipient,              # byte string, exactly 20 bytes
68	  prev_randao,                # byte string, exactly 32 bytes
69	  gas_limit,                  # positive u64
70	  extra_data,                 # byte string, 0..32 bytes
71	  cancun_parent_beacon_root   # byte string, exactly 32 bytes
72	]
73	
74	ordinary_record := [empty_gap, kind, data]
75	kind 0: data := [signed_tx_bytes, ...]   # nonempty, Bytes / EIP-2718
76	kind 1: data := canonical_full_block_rlp # one Bytes value, exact RLP
77	```
78	
79	`empty_gap` is the number of default empty ordinary blocks since the preceding
80	record, or since the anchor for the first record. After the gap, the record consumes
81	one block. Remaining positions up to `ordinary_block_count` are default empty
82	blocks. For example, count 100 and a transaction record with gap 99 puts that
83	record in ordinary position 99, using zero-based positions. No record encodes an
84	empty transaction list; an empty exception uses a full-block record. Records
85	cannot overlap, run backwards, or consume the terminal position.
86	
87	Counts and integers use canonical unsigned RLP. Reject negative/oversized integer
88	representations, noncanonical RLP, wrong list arity, trailing bytes, unknown tags,
89	unsupported profile IDs/kinds, malformed transaction/block encodings, arithmetic
90	overflow and record coverage beyond the declared count. Apply the block ceiling
91	before allocations or expansion. Retain the existing per-block transaction-count
92	bound (`u16::MAX`) and fork-aware transaction validity. Bound list parsing by the
93	actual input slice; do not allocate from unchecked declared RLP lengths.
94	
95	No arbitrary data-byte expansion is needed during parsing: keep sparse records
96	and borrowed/owned input slices. A bounded block-plan iterator produces ordinary
97	positions. Arrays of block counts may contain at most 65,536 elements; full headers
98	are built by execution, not synthesized by the codec.
99	
100	The 65,536 format bound applies to tag `0x03`; do not add a retroactive validity
101	restriction to historical tags. Operational signer request limits remain separate.
102	
103	The batch's effective anchor/range remains established by existing settlement
104	logic. The payload count must agree with the proof window and placement rules.
105	Do not introduce a second source of authority for the starting block hash.
106	
107	### 3.1 Common environment and full-block exceptions
108	
109	The composer builds the common environment from its actual sequencing inputs;
110	the environment is published and bound by DA. It is not inferred from the
111	follower's local operator defaults. The signer checks it against every block
112	represented by the derived path. A different but valid environment can therefore
113	be represented without silently changing a block.
114	
115	For a derived block:
116	
117	- Number is the parent's number plus one, with checked arithmetic.
118	- Timestamp is the parent's timestamp plus the explicit positive step, with
119	  checked arithmetic. The step must reproduce the validated block's actual
120	  timestamp; it is not permission to violate active consensus timestamp rules.
121	- Use the explicit fee recipient, randomness, gas limit and extra data.
122	- Pre-Cancun parent beacon root is absent. From Cancun onward use the explicit
123	  root in the common environment. This permits the current zero input without
124	  treating zero as an undocumented consensus constant.
125	- Ommers are empty. Withdrawals are absent before Shanghai and empty afterward.
126	- Parent hash, execution outputs and remaining header values come from the
127	  authenticated parent, chain rules and actual execution.
128	
129	Support the pinned execution stack's post-Merge rules through Osaka initially,
130	including supported boundaries within that range. Profile 1 does not derive
131	pre-Merge blocks, blocks with nonempty withdrawals/ommers, or blocks requiring
132	newer slot-number/block-access-list fields. Such ordinary blocks must use full
133	records if the existing execution stack can validate them; otherwise reject them
134	as unsupported. A future execution-fork upgrade must add profile conformance
135	tests or explicitly retain full records, never silently extend defaults.
136	
137	An ordinary block that differs in timestamp, environment, body shape or any
138	reconstructed header field uses a full record. The following block derives from
139	that full block's actual header. The encoder prefers derivation when its complete
140	eligibility check succeeds; readers may accept an otherwise valid full record
141	even when a shorter representation would have been possible. Full-record
142	acceptance still enforces the existing ordinary/system-sender restrictions.
143	
144	For a terminal-only range, retain the normal common environment chosen by the
145	writer; it is syntactically checked but has no ordinary execution effect.
146	
147	## 4. One execution-input interpretation, independent execution checks
148	
149	Introduce a typed `OrdinaryExecutionInputs` and `BlockPlan` in
150	`eez-payload-codec`; add the shared translation/assembly helper under
151	`eez-driver::derivation` (feature-gated as needed). Signer and follower already
152	depend on the driver. Avoid a dependency cycle or a second hand-written Ethereum
153	header implementation.
154	
155	Use the pinned Reth `EthBlockAssembler` and next-block environment construction.
156	Its assembler builds transaction/receipt/withdrawal roots, bloom, gas fields,
157	requests hash and the other header fields from parent, execution context and
158	execution outputs. Expose the minimal adapter inputs needed to call that same
159	assembler from signer validation. Do not copy roots from a submitted header into
160	the reconstruction and call that derivation.
161	
162	### 4.1 Signer
163	
164	The signer still receives complete block RLP and witnesses during cold validation
165	or ordinary preparation. Existing Stateless validation authenticates execution,
166	state roots, transaction signatures and witness pre-state. For each derived
167	ordinary block it must additionally:
168	
169	1. Obtain and authenticate the parent header against the block's parent hash,
170	   using the accepted prior block or witness ancestor for the first block.
171	2. Construct the EVM environment from that parent, the recipe and trusted chain
172	   rules. Confirm it matches the environment used for the validated execution.
173	3. Assemble the complete block using that environment, the exact transaction list,
174	   and the successful Stateless output (state root, receipts, requests and gas).
175	   The current backend exposes these outputs before reducing them to settlement
176	   facts; perform the check there rather than discarding them prematurely.
177	4. Require byte-for-byte canonical full-block RLP equality with the validated
178	   original block. Check no intermediate system-sender transaction is admitted.
179	5. Preserve window parent-hash continuity and state-root telescoping. Keep all
180	   existing terminal checkpoints, lookup observations and settlement gates.
181	
182	This validates the omitted header outputs, not just inputs or transaction lists.
183	Full ordinary exceptions take the existing exact full-block path. The terminal
184	always takes the existing checkpoint-capable path. DA/semantic binding and
185	public-input recomputation still precede attestation.
186	
187	### 4.2 Follower
188	
189	Refactor `execute_block_with_template` into an execution-input path plus the
190	existing full-template validation wrapper. A derived block has an explicit
191	recipe; it must not appear as a fake full template with zero output fields, or
192	fall accidentally into the old no-template default branch.
193	
194	Run all pre-execution transitions, transactions and post-execution transitions,
195	including for empty gaps. Build every intervening block so `BLOCKHASH`, system
196	contract state, base fee and fork transitions remain correct. Reuse locally
197	present blocks only if the existing ancestry and new recipe/environment checks
198	establish equivalence; matching transaction lists alone is insufficient.
199	
200	Keep terminal reconstruction, source authorization, partial settlement,
201	same-height resume and `check_claimed_state` behavior. The L1-applied endpoint may
202	be a prefix of the advertised Sync; do not replace it with the last root claimed
203	in calldata. New-format metadata must also flow through catch-up, correlation,
204	batch evidence, restart and safe/finalized-head paths, not only live replay.
205	
206	No signer cache is needed or trusted by a follower. A clean follower must derive
207	from the canonical anchor, available L1/DA inputs and chain configuration alone.
208	
209	## 5. Incremental signer validation for long spans
210	
211	Increasing the block ceiling alone would leave the whole ordinary history to be
212	re-executed inside a Sync deadline. Include incremental validation in this plan,
213	using the existing persistent per-block witness store as the producer-side source.
214	It changes internal proving work, not what cross-chain settlement authorizes.
215	
216	### 5.1 Internal RPC extensions
217	
218	Add backward-compatible methods to `prove.v1.Prover` and an additional Prove
219	chunk variant; retain existing message numbers and semantics:
220	
221	- `Capabilities`: supported operations/profile versions, activation timestamp,
222	  maximum total window blocks, request bytes/witness items, preparation chunk
223	  ceiling, effective per-message limit, timeout values, and validation identity.
224	  The identity binds rollup ID, EIP-155 chain ID, chain/fork configuration digest,
225	  expected system address and a validator-schema/revision identifier. It does not
226	  expose private keys.
227	- `PrepareOrdinary(stream ...)`: complete ordinary block RLP/witnesses, in bounded
228	  chunks, with expected common environment and parent linkage. It performs actual
229	  Stateless validation and the §4.1 recipe equivalence checks. Return only the
230	  verified block hashes and the current cache generation; **never a settlement
231	  signature or a safe-head claim**.
232	- `CachedOrdinaryBlock` Prove chunk: number, block hash, parent hash and cache
233	  generation. It resolves only to locally validated immutable facts. A hash or
234	  token supplied by the composer is not evidence by itself.
235	
236	The final `Prove` request may mix cached ordinary references and fully witnessed
237	ordinary blocks, but the terminal is always fully witnessed and freshly checked.
238	Every logical block counts against the total window ceiling even if it uses a
239	reference. Unknown/evicted references return a structured retryable cache-miss
240	result with the missing block identity, not an actionable cross-chain failure.
241	
242	Preparation uses a header-first stream: rollup ID, expected validation identity
243	and proposed common environment, followed by ascending `BlockWitness` values.
244	It requires a nonempty contiguous ordinary range, at most 64 blocks. Each block's
245	parent is authenticated by its witness or the preceding validated header; no
246	client-supplied state-root shortcut is accepted. A fully validated ordinary block
247	that needs the full-record path can be cached too, marked ineligible for derived
248	use under that environment. Preparation failures return no reference for a failed
249	block; successfully validated immutable earlier facts may remain cached and can
250	be discovered/reused on retry. No partly validated entry is ever published.
251	
252	Capability calls do not acquire the expensive execution permit. Preparation
253	streams have bounded ingestion queues and may not hold that permit while waiting
254	for more network input. Admission of a final proof preempts preparation between
255	block executions; one already-running block may finish, which is included in the
256	deadline tests. Retain the existing single active final-proof admission behavior.
257	
258	Use `UNAVAILABLE` with a new structured cache-miss detail for missing references;
259	include generation and first missing block identity. The remote client invalidates
260	those references and schedules bounded preparation. It does not turn a cache miss
261	into eviction of a cross-chain source or repeatedly send the same unresolved
262	reference through `prove_with_retry`. If repair cannot fit the current target,
263	follow the existing unsent/failed-attempt reconciliation rules and keep ownership.
264	Malformed references and mismatched block identities are validation errors, not
265	cache misses that can be repaired by guessing another block.
266	
267	Capabilities are advisory for resource planning, not cryptographic authority.
268	The existing returned-signature/public-input verification remains authoritative.
269	Recheck capabilities at connection/reconnection. A v3-enabled composer requires a
270	compatible signer; it must not guess limits when the endpoint is unavailable.
271	Legacy operation can use an old signer only with v3 emission disabled and an
272	explicitly compatible existing configuration.
273	
274	### 5.2 Cache identity and integrity
275	
276	Key cached facts by full block hash and validation identity. Store canonical block
277	RLP, authenticated parent/header facts, pre/post-state commitments, ordinary
278	system-sender classification and the verified derivation inputs. Different recipe
279	inputs must be checked against those exact facts; a validation for one environment
280	does not authorize another. Never key validity by height alone.
281	
282	On final proof, verify the exact linked sequence, pre/post-state telescoping,
283	recipe match, requested terminal parent and all existing settlement binding.
284	Cached blocks can belong to another fork; their hashes are reusable facts, but
285	their place in this request is checked anew. Cached validation never marks data
286	canonical or settled.
287	
288	Use a volatile byte-accounted cache with default ceilings **131,072 entries and
289	512 MiB of retained data/accounted metadata**, whichever is reached first. Include
290	an allowance for map/node overhead in accounting and separately measure process
291	RSS. Pin entries only while admitting/validating an active request. Evict unpinned
292	LRU entries; if space cannot be obtained, reject preparation before allocation.
293	Do not evict a referenced block halfway through an admitted proof.
294	
295	A fresh process has a new cache generation. Restart invalidates references and
296	triggers bounded re-preparation from the existing durable witness store. A chain
297	configuration or validator revision change invalidates the whole namespace.
298	Cache loss is a performance event, not permission to sign unchecked data.
299	
300	### 5.3 Scheduling, cancellation and storage
301	
302	Prepare after a committed ordinary block's witness is durable. Default preparation
303	chunks contain at most **64 blocks**, additionally bounded by current byte/item
304	quotas; adapt to fewer blocks when needed. A single oversized block is reported
305	explicitly. Keep the preparation queue bounded and deduplicate by block hash.
306	
307	Set the producer's preparation queue to at most 128 block identities; on overload
308	keep a canonical catch-up watermark instead of accumulating witnesses in RAM.
309	After catching up, verify the watermark's hash and rewind it to matching ancestry
310	after reorgs. Preparation drains from the existing durable witness store. A
311	separate lightweight reference index may span the bounded pending history, but
312	must not retain a second witness copy.
313	
314	Use one shared validation worker/permit as today. Final proof requests have
315	priority at block boundaries; ordinary preparation checks cancellation between
316	blocks and cannot indefinitely starve a terminal proof. Streaming ingestion and
317	cache admission are also quota-bound. Timeout/cancellation must release permits,
318	pins and buffers; signing after deadline/cancellation remains forbidden.
319	
320	Before selecting cross-chain work for an exact slot, require the ordinary prefix
321	to be prepared or demonstrably cold-validatable within the remaining budget.
322	Otherwise prewarm and use the existing readiness deferral; never move already
323	selected cross-chain effects to a different target or relax submission slack.
324	Keep owned sources queued. An anchor-only candidate may use the existing eligible
325	future-target selection after preparation; it is still bound to the final target
326	when signing.
327	
328	Change composer witness assembly and `RemoteProver::chunks_for` to use lightweight
329	references for prepared ordinary blocks and move/stream full witnesses for cache
330	misses and the terminal. Do not build duplicate full-window witness vectors.
331	Retain witnesses durably until the existing L1-finalized purge floor. Verify
332	hashes on store hits, including after reorgs, exactly as the current witness source
333	does. Disk-full/missing-witness conditions fail closed and must not silently prune
334	unsettled history. The existing MDBX map ceiling is not a free-disk guarantee.
335	
336	## 6. Encoding and resource accounting in the composer
337	
338	Implement `DerivablePayloadSizer` beside the codec. The same shape definitions
339	must drive exact encoding and sizing; no empirical compression ratios are allowed.
340	It accounts for common environment, count/list prefixes, sparse record gaps,
341	transactions, full exceptions, unchanged terminal/entries/groups, and native
342	message framing/semantics.
343	
344	Replace the old full-block item prefix accounting for v3. The activity index needs
345	a composable range summary containing block count, first/last record positions,
346	encoded record data lengths, gap-prefix lengths, and transaction activity. On
347	re-anchoring adjust the first record's gap; when a historical endpoint becomes
348	the terminal remove its ordinary representation and add its unchanged full
349	terminal representation. Simply subtracting old encoded-byte prefix sums is wrong.
350	Index/cache identity includes format, profile, environment digest and anchor/hash.
351	Reorgs rewind to matching ancestry; configuration changes invalidate summaries.
352	
353	Use exact completed-record sizes and conservative bounds for unknown future
354	inputs. Derived ordinary blocks no longer reserve unknown output-root/bloom bytes.
355	Full exceptions and the future terminal still use full-block bounds. Account for
356	integer/list-prefix growth and worst-case explicit exception records before
357	admitting a transaction. Check the actual final encoding before committing a
358	newly built block/candidate; retain overflow transactions and nonce dependencies.
359	Keep active/future-fork blob maxima and companion consumption checks.
360	
361	Update both ordinary pool admission/interval guards and final candidate sizing.
362	Preserve legal empty Sync boundaries used to split retained history. Include
363	logical block ceilings, signer capabilities and exact request-resource estimates
364	in feasible-prefix selection. A pending prefix must have a legal endpoint before
365	any applicable hard limit; reserve through that boundary. If no single legal
366	interval fits, reject startup/admission with a specific error rather than accepting
367	history that cannot settle. Existing incompatible retained history must be kept
368	and reported, never truncated.
369	
370	Local resource failure may split ordinary history only at existing legal boundaries
371	and cannot split a cross-chain group. Missing/stale capability data pauses dependent
372	admission until refreshed. A lowered signer limit is detected before dispatch;
373	already accepted history drains through feasible historical prefixes where possible.
374	
375	## 7. Defaults and the meaning of “large enough”
376	
377	| Limit | Planned default / behavior |
378	|---|---|
379	| Signer total blocks per request | **65,536**, replacing 512; operator override retained. |
380	| V3 format maximum total blocks | **65,536**, enforced by every decoder, independent of local operational caps. |
381	| Aggregate Prove/Prepare request bytes | Existing **512 MiB**; references are charged by their encoded request size, cached data remains bounded separately. |
382	| Aggregate streamed witness-array items | Existing **1,000,000** per request; every cold block is validated, across as many bounded preparations as required. |
383	| Effective server message maximum | Existing **256 MiB**, or a smaller request limit; client honors the advertised maximum instead of assuming its current 1 GiB setting is accepted. |
384	| Stream idle / total request deadline | Existing **120 / 600 seconds**; target-slot deadline takes precedence for final posting. |
385	| Preparation chunk | At most **64 blocks**, further reduced by byte/item limits. |
386	| Validation concurrency | One worker, terminal priority between blocks; no concurrent unbounded warmup. |
387	| Signer cached facts | At most **131,072 entries / 512 MiB accounted memory**. |
388	
389	These are implementation decisions. Validation must show they meet the targeted
390	empty/light-history workloads. If the acceptance workload cannot be prepared or
391	proved under these limits, the release gate fails: fix the implementation or amend
392	the explicit, reviewed resource envelope and rerun tests. Do not quietly claim
393	65,536 usable blocks after testing only header admission.
394	
395	Signer reference resolution remains bounded by the same total-block maximum;
396	preparing blocks in several calls must not bypass the final request's count cap.
397	On-chain follower acceptance uses format/consensus limits, not another operator's
398	RPC/cache settings. A follower with insufficient local resources reports inability
399	to sync, not a different validity rule for an otherwise valid batch.
400	
401	Existing ordinary time/count posting triggers and speculative-depth configuration
402	remain effective. Document configurations that allow the intended multi-hour
403	history and validate their consistency with the signer and legal grid. Do not
404	silently increase latency settings or disable cross-chain due rules.
405	
406	## 8. Activation, history and rollback
407	
408	Add one coordinated setting, `EEZ_CHAIN_OPERATION_V3_ACTIVATION_TIMESTAMP`, an
409	unsigned L2 Unix timestamp. Absence disables v3 acceptance/emission. Persist it
410	with the deployment's reviewed chain/runtime configuration and expose it in signer
411	capabilities. All readers/signers/writers must agree before activation. This is a
412	proposed setting to implement, not an existing supported option.
413	
414	V3 eligibility is decided by the timestamp of its retained full terminal header,
415	which the signer validates and the follower binds through the existing settlement
416	path. Earlier ordinary history may cross the activation timestamp because every
417	ordinary position explicitly selects a supported derivation or full-block path.
418	Reject v3 with a terminal before activation. Keep old formats valid afterward so
419	historical replay and writer rollback remain possible. Never reinterpret old data.
420	
421	Rollout order: shared codec/replay support and tests; readers and signer; capability
422	and configuration checks; writer activation at the selected future timestamp.
423	Run a clean follower through pre/post-activation history before declaring success.
424	Deployment commands are a later operational task, not part of this plan execution.
425	
426	Rollback disables new writer emission while retaining v3 readers. Restore a
427	previous writer only if it includes v3 historical decoding and can drain retained
428	history using legal legacy-sized prefixes. Never roll a reader back to a binary
429	unable to read already settled v3 data. Retain witness storage, checkpoints and
430	canonical history; no chain reset or data rewrite.
431	
432	## 9. Work packages and ownership by component
433	
434	| Order | Components | Deliverable / dependency |
435	|---|---|---|
436	| A | `eez-payload-codec`; proposal/golden fixtures | Exact v3 types, parser, encoder, iterator, size algebra and bounded decode; legacy fixtures unchanged. |
437	| B | `eez-driver::derivation`; pinned Reth adapter; `eez-proof-signer/validate/stateless.rs` | Shared execution inputs and ordinary full-block reconstruction from validated outputs. Depends on A. |
438	| C | `eez-deriver` live/catch-up/reconciliation/correlation; `eez-l1` evidence/example tools | New block plans throughout follower and tooling; preserve terminal and L1-applied endpoint gates. Depends on B. |
439	| D | `eez-proof-signer/settlement/da.rs`, service/limits/config; `SPEC.md` | V3 recipe-to-window checks, terminal binding unchanged, 65,536 default, bounded count/resource failures. Depends on B. |
440	| E | `eez-control-rpc/proto/prove.proto`, generated modules; `eez-prover`, `eez-prover-client`, signer service/cache | Capabilities, PrepareOrdinary, cached references, quota/cancellation/priority behavior. Depends on D. |
441	| F | `eez-node` proving/witness integration; composer proof-context construction | Durable-witness-triggered preparation, bounded retry/restart/reorg behavior, eliminate duplicate witness-window allocations. Depends on E. |
442	| G | `eez-composer` policy/index/sequencing/admission/encoding; `eez-node-common` payload/pool sizing | Exact v3 estimates, terminal promotion, feasible prefixes, capability checks and overflow prevention. Depends on A, E, F. |
443	| H | Composer/signer/follower launch configuration and deployment templates | Shared activation setting, compatibility checks, rollout and rollback instructions. Depends on C–G. |
444	| I | `eez-node-e2e`, signer integration tests, CI and research artifacts | Complete equivalence/adversarial/performance evidence and operator capacity envelope. Release depends on all gates. |
445	
446	Review in these bounded packages; no package may silently change the wire shape or
447	shared defaults. A discovered omission updates this specification and its coverage
448	row before implementation proceeds. Production activation remains disabled until
449	package I passes.
450	
451	The initial requirement-to-component mapping is in the
452	[coverage ledger](derivable-chain-operations-coverage.md). Every entry starts as
453	planned; implementation must replace that status with code and evidence links.
454	
455	## 10. Correctness and failure coverage
456	
457	| Area | Required cases and assertions |
458	|---|---|
459	| Codec | Empty ordinary range; one/65,535 ordinary blocks; reject 65,536 ordinary blocks; RLP prefix boundaries; malformed/truncated/overflow inputs; unknown tags/profile/kind; gaps past end; extra records; wrong terminal count; signed transaction byte identity. |
460	| Scope preservation | Compare encoded terminal, entries, group sizes and outer semantic suffix byte-for-byte before/after. Verify the same physical packing rules and public-input/KZG binding. |
461	| Derived execution | Empty/nonempty/reverted blocks; legacy/2930/1559/7702 and every other currently accepted transaction type; block boundaries and ordering; zero and changed environment; fallback before/after derived blocks; contract reads of NUMBER/TIMESTAMP/COINBASE/PREVRANDAO/GASLIMIT/BASEFEE/BLOCKHASH; pre/post-execution system transitions. |
462	| Forks | All currently supported post-Merge L2 configurations, first Shanghai/Cancun/Prague/Osaka blocks where applicable, supported boundary crossing, optional field presence, future unsupported profile transition uses full records or rejects. |
463	| Signer tampering | Valid txs with altered environment/count/gap; header outputs differing from assembly; wrong parent/config; system sender hidden as ordinary; missing transactions; wrong terminal/entry binding; no attestation on any mismatch. |
464	| Settlement | Full, partial, deferred, reverted, resumed and competing same-L1-block paths; canonical applied-prefix endpoint, outbound event gate and value effects unchanged. Include terminal-only and fallback ranges. |
465	| Cache trust | Wrong block/height/parent/environment/generation/config; stale fork, eviction before/after pinning, corrupt/missing entries, reused reference in incompatible window; cold and cached results identical. Cache cannot authorize system transactions or terminal observations. |
466	| Resources | Every quota boundary; count checked before expansion; Prepare chunks cannot evade final count; cache accounting includes overhead; cancellation/timeout releases memory/permits; cold validation and preparation cannot starve final proof. |
467	| Persistence/reorg | Node/signer restarts with pruned parent state; rebuild from durable witnesses; witness hash mismatch; no purge above finalized floor; L1 rollback and alternate L2 ancestry; reader catch-up without producer RPC. |
468	| Sizing | Encoded size equals estimate for completed candidates; conservative future reservation; new first gap on re-anchor; ordinary-to-terminal promotion; historical splits; all RLP thresholds; next-nonce preservation and individually unpostable transactions. |
469	| Operational limits | Lower signer/operator limits, capability unavailability/reconnect/change, stale target slot, missing witness, disk/cache full; retain owned sources and accepted history with explicit bounded recovery. |
470	| Compatibility | Old tags/old fixtures; old signer with v3 disabled; incompatible signer prevents v3 launch; before/at/after activation; retained-v3 writer rollback; clean follower through mixed formats. |
471	
472	Run affected unit/integration tests, the existing native settlement/cross-chain
473	suite on Ethereum and Gnosis profiles, all-target Clippy, formatting and whitespace
474	checks. Unit round trips do not substitute for independent follower execution.
475	Use property tests for record/gap size composition and parser bounds and fuzz the
476	new parser/iterator, including maximal declared runs with minimal input.
477	
478	## 11. Performance gates and evidence
479	
480	Use fixed chain configuration and immutable transaction inputs. Compare old full
481	blocks, the new recipe with cold proof validation, and the prepared-reference path.
482	Measure physical blob counts from actual final encodings, not corpus-wide sums.
483	
484	Required span sizes: **512, 1,024, 4,096, 10,000, 43,200 and 65,536 total blocks**.
485	For each, exercise empty history and a sparse deterministic transfer workload that
486	fits the same six-blob example allowance; also run boundary-filling and high-entropy
487	data workloads whose expected result may be a smaller feasible prefix. Do not
488	claim every workload should fit 65,536 blocks. Account for the unchanged terminal
489	and semantic bytes explicitly.
490	
491	Required measurable outcomes:
492	
493	1. A 43,200-block empty-history candidate and a 65,536-block empty-history
494	   candidate encode within the actual allowed blob count, with no per-empty-block
495	   header bytes. They independently replay to exact original block hashes.
496	2. The signer accepts the fully valid largest-window example with the planned
497	   defaults using bounded preparation, and rejects 65,537 total blocks. The
498	   terminal still receives full fresh validation.
499	3. Prepared-path final proof plus remaining preparation fits the configured
500	   submission deadline for both native L1 profiles in the test environment; record
501	   at least 20 warm repetitions, median/p95/max and misses. All repetitions must
502	   fit the release profile's deadline; no fixed hardware-independent seconds are
503	   invented in this plan. Cold recovery times are reported separately.
504	4. Existing cross-chain latency/deadline tests remain passing under concurrent
505	   background preparation. No group changes target, order or semantic bytes to
506	   achieve the timing result.
507	5. Record peak composer/signer/follower RSS, cache-accounted bytes, witness DB
508	   growth, request bytes/items, disk reads and cache hit/miss rates. Cache and
509	   request quotas must hold under adversarial and cancellation cases; the report
510	   specifies the minimum tested machine resources and configuration.
511	6. Steady-state block accounting/preparation processes new work incrementally;
512	   no full-history rescans each L2 tick or full witness copies at each proof retry.
513	   Document catch-up/reorg costs separately.
514	
515	Emit structured measurements keyed by anchor hash, candidate terminal hash and,
516	after dispatch, postBatch hash. Include payload/profile versions, ordinary total,
517	derived-empty/nonempty/full-exception counts, unchanged terminal/entry/semantic
518	bytes, encoded stream bytes, actual blobs, cache hit/miss counts, witness request
519	bytes/items, preparation/proof/replay times, and the precise limiting constraint.
520	Do not count retries as additional settled capacity. Never log witness contents,
521	private keys or full user transaction data merely to measure their lengths.
522	
523	If any required gate fails, the implementation is not complete. Resolve the
524	failure without reducing scope, weakening verification, dropping cross-chain tests
525	or silently lowering the claimed supported empty-history span. Any proposed
526	resource/default or architecture amendment is recorded and revalidated explicitly.
527	
528	Artifacts include repository/dependency/binary identities, activation/configuration,
529	input hashes, per-block replay comparisons, receipt/commitment checks, byte tables,
530	timing/memory logs and exact reproduction commands. The final operator guide
531	separates the 65,536 format/default ceiling from measured transaction-volume and
532	hardware-dependent capacity.
533	
534	## 12. Definition of done
535	
536	- Every normative rule above has an implementation and test/evidence link in a
537	  checked-in coverage ledger; no unassigned design questions or missing rows.
538	- New on-chain data differs only within `ChainOperation.operations` and consequent
539	  carrier lengths/commitments. All original blocks and cross-chain results agree.
540	- Full history is derivable by an independent follower from authenticated inputs;
541	  no local signer cache or sequencer header service becomes a DA dependency.
542	- Signer defaults, preparation, admission and posting deadlines support the tested
543	  long-empty-history spans without relocating cross-chain effects or accepting
544	  unbounded work.
545	- Backward compatibility, partial settlement, reorg, restart, activation and writer
546	  rollback are verified; no live deployment is implied by finishing the code.
547	
548	This plan removes unowned implementation decisions. It does not assert that
549	untested code has no defects; the release gates are how the remaining empirical
550	questions are resolved before the change is considered complete.

# Derivable ChainOperation: implementation contract

Status: proposed implementation plan, 2026-09-16. Reviewed against
`ddf40bc2eb5fac8f7973b112eb383256cd8aac74`. No runtime change or deployment is
performed by this document. It supersedes the ordering in the exploratory
[research](../research/2026-09-16-blob-efficiency/README.md).

## 1. Objective and fixed scope

Fit substantially more ordinary L2 history in one permitted blob transaction by
publishing execution inputs rather than complete ordinary blocks. Empty ordinary
blocks must not contribute a header-sized DA cost. Follower execution must produce
the original blocks and match the commitment actually applied on L1.

Only `ChainOperation.operations` changes on the DA wire. Preserve:

- The standardized outer message version, semantic messages, signed cross-chain
  transaction bytes, call/result/rollback data, and message order.
- The terminal Sync block's existing encoding and all `l2_entries` and
  `outbound_group_sizes` encodings, values, and order.
- Physical blob packing, KZG and public-input binding, contract ABI/storage,
  ECDSA/proof-system semantics and cross-chain scheduling/ownership rules.
- Existing historical payload decoding and independent follower validation.

No zlib, Brotli, or other general-purpose compression. No cross-chain deduplication,
new calldata carrier, shared blob channel, hash truncation, or omitted system
transaction is part of this change. Internal proving RPC extensions and signer
limits are in scope because long spans must be usable at settlement time.

## 2. Decisions

| Decision | Specification |
|---|---|
| New inner payload tag | `0x03`, named `TAG_DERIVABLE_ORDINARY`. Existing tags `0x00..0x02` retain their exact meanings. Research-only hypothetical tags were never production assignments. |
| First profile | `profile_id = 1`: derive supported post-Merge ordinary Ethereum blocks using explicit common execution inputs; retain full-block exceptions. |
| Terminal treatment | Always exactly one full terminal block, with the old integer-list encoding intact. Never apply ordinary omission rules to it. |
| Ordinary representation | Total count, common environment, sparse records for nonempty/exception blocks; gaps mean empty blocks executed under that environment. |
| Format block ceiling | 65,536 total blocks, including the terminal. Thus at most 65,535 ordinary blocks per v3 payload. This is a format safety bound. |
| Signer block default | Change `EEZ_PROOF_SIGNER_MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS` from 512 to **65,536**. Explicit lower operator values remain effective for local admission. |
| Other signer quotas | Keep current bounded byte/item/time defaults, detailed in §7. Do not multiply all quotas by the block-count increase. Incremental validation and cached references handle long ordinary history. |
| Long-span validation | Prepare and validate ordinary blocks ahead of settlement; reference immutable signer-local validated facts at final proving. Terminal validation remains fresh. |
| Activation | Coordinated timestamp-gated v3 reader/writer support, with legacy payload acceptance retained. No fixed calendar date is selected by the implementation. |

65,536 blocks span about 36 h 24 min at two seconds per block. This is an admission
ceiling, not a claim that 36 hours of arbitrary transactions fits DA, memory or
execution budgets. The supported workload envelope is established by §11.

## 3. Exact v3 data shape

Use canonical Ethereum RLP and explicitly typed Rust `Bytes` for new opaque byte
strings. Do not rely on `Vec<u8>` to encode a byte string. Preserve the legacy
types for the three unchanged terminal/cross-chain fields.

```text
0x03 || rlp([
  profile_id,                 # integer, exactly 1
  ordinary_block_count,       # integer, 0..65535
  common_environment,        # fixed-arity list below
  ordinary_records,          # ordered list below
  terminal_block_legacy,     # old Vec<u8> integer-list item, exact original bytes
  l2_entries_legacy,          # old Vec<Vec<u8>> representation, unchanged
  outbound_group_sizes       # old Vec<u16> representation, unchanged
])

common_environment := [
  timestamp_step_seconds,     # nonzero u64
  fee_recipient,              # byte string, exactly 20 bytes
  prev_randao,                # byte string, exactly 32 bytes
  gas_limit,                  # positive u64
  extra_data,                 # byte string, 0..32 bytes
  cancun_parent_beacon_root   # byte string, exactly 32 bytes
]

ordinary_record := [empty_gap, kind, data]
kind 0: data := [signed_tx_bytes, ...]   # nonempty, Bytes / EIP-2718
kind 1: data := canonical_full_block_rlp # one Bytes value, exact RLP
```

`empty_gap` is the number of default empty ordinary blocks since the preceding
record, or since the anchor for the first record. After the gap, the record consumes
one block. Remaining positions up to `ordinary_block_count` are default empty
blocks. For example, count 100 and a transaction record with gap 99 puts that
record in ordinary position 99, using zero-based positions. No record encodes an
empty transaction list; an empty exception uses a full-block record. Records
cannot overlap, run backwards, or consume the terminal position.

Counts and integers use canonical unsigned RLP. Reject negative/oversized integer
representations, noncanonical RLP, wrong list arity, trailing bytes, unknown tags,
unsupported profile IDs/kinds, malformed transaction/block encodings, arithmetic
overflow and record coverage beyond the declared count. Apply the block ceiling
before allocations or expansion. Retain the existing per-block transaction-count
bound (`u16::MAX`) and fork-aware transaction validity. Bound list parsing by the
actual input slice; do not allocate from unchecked declared RLP lengths.

No arbitrary data-byte expansion is needed during parsing: keep sparse records
and borrowed/owned input slices. A bounded block-plan iterator produces ordinary
positions. Arrays of block counts may contain at most 65,536 elements; full headers
are built by execution, not synthesized by the codec.

The 65,536 format bound applies to tag `0x03`; do not add a retroactive validity
restriction to historical tags. Operational signer request limits remain separate.

The batch's effective anchor/range remains established by existing settlement
logic. The payload count must agree with the proof window and placement rules.
Do not introduce a second source of authority for the starting block hash.

### 3.1 Common environment and full-block exceptions

The composer builds the common environment from its actual sequencing inputs;
the environment is published and bound by DA. It is not inferred from the
follower's local operator defaults. The signer checks it against every block
represented by the derived path. A different but valid environment can therefore
be represented without silently changing a block.

For a derived block:

- Number is the parent's number plus one, with checked arithmetic.
- Timestamp is the parent's timestamp plus the explicit positive step, with
  checked arithmetic. The step must reproduce the validated block's actual
  timestamp; it is not permission to violate active consensus timestamp rules.
- Use the explicit fee recipient, randomness, gas limit and extra data.
- Pre-Cancun parent beacon root is absent. From Cancun onward use the explicit
  root in the common environment. This permits the current zero input without
  treating zero as an undocumented consensus constant.
- Ommers are empty. Withdrawals are absent before Shanghai and empty afterward.
- Parent hash, execution outputs and remaining header values come from the
  authenticated parent, chain rules and actual execution.

Support the pinned execution stack's post-Merge rules through Osaka initially,
including supported boundaries within that range. Profile 1 does not derive
pre-Merge blocks, blocks with nonempty withdrawals/ommers, or blocks requiring
newer slot-number/block-access-list fields. Such ordinary blocks must use full
records if the existing execution stack can validate them; otherwise reject them
as unsupported. A future execution-fork upgrade must add profile conformance
tests or explicitly retain full records, never silently extend defaults.

An ordinary block that differs in timestamp, environment, body shape or any
reconstructed header field uses a full record. The following block derives from
that full block's actual header. The encoder prefers derivation when its complete
eligibility check succeeds; readers may accept an otherwise valid full record
even when a shorter representation would have been possible. Full-record
acceptance still enforces the existing ordinary/system-sender restrictions.

For a terminal-only range, retain the normal common environment chosen by the
writer; it is syntactically checked but has no ordinary execution effect.

## 4. One execution-input interpretation, independent execution checks

Introduce a typed `OrdinaryExecutionInputs` and `BlockPlan` in
`eez-payload-codec`; add the shared translation/assembly helper under
`eez-driver::derivation` (feature-gated as needed). Signer and follower already
depend on the driver. Avoid a dependency cycle or a second hand-written Ethereum
header implementation.

Use the pinned Reth `EthBlockAssembler` and next-block environment construction.
Its assembler builds transaction/receipt/withdrawal roots, bloom, gas fields,
requests hash and the other header fields from parent, execution context and
execution outputs. Expose the minimal adapter inputs needed to call that same
assembler from signer validation. Do not copy roots from a submitted header into
the reconstruction and call that derivation.

### 4.1 Signer

The signer still receives complete block RLP and witnesses during cold validation
or ordinary preparation. Existing Stateless validation authenticates execution,
state roots, transaction signatures and witness pre-state. For each derived
ordinary block it must additionally:

1. Obtain and authenticate the parent header against the block's parent hash,
   using the accepted prior block or witness ancestor for the first block.
2. Construct the EVM environment from that parent, the recipe and trusted chain
   rules. Confirm it matches the environment used for the validated execution.
3. Assemble the complete block using that environment, the exact transaction list,
   and the successful Stateless output (state root, receipts, requests and gas).
   The current backend exposes these outputs before reducing them to settlement
   facts; perform the check there rather than discarding them prematurely.
4. Require byte-for-byte canonical full-block RLP equality with the validated
   original block. Check no intermediate system-sender transaction is admitted.
5. Preserve window parent-hash continuity and state-root telescoping. Keep all
   existing terminal checkpoints, lookup observations and settlement gates.

This validates the omitted header outputs, not just inputs or transaction lists.
Full ordinary exceptions take the existing exact full-block path. The terminal
always takes the existing checkpoint-capable path. DA/semantic binding and
public-input recomputation still precede attestation.

### 4.2 Follower

Refactor `execute_block_with_template` into an execution-input path plus the
existing full-template validation wrapper. A derived block has an explicit
recipe; it must not appear as a fake full template with zero output fields, or
fall accidentally into the old no-template default branch.

Run all pre-execution transitions, transactions and post-execution transitions,
including for empty gaps. Build every intervening block so `BLOCKHASH`, system
contract state, base fee and fork transitions remain correct. Reuse locally
present blocks only if the existing ancestry and new recipe/environment checks
establish equivalence; matching transaction lists alone is insufficient.

Keep terminal reconstruction, source authorization, partial settlement,
same-height resume and `check_claimed_state` behavior. The L1-applied endpoint may
be a prefix of the advertised Sync; do not replace it with the last root claimed
in calldata. New-format metadata must also flow through catch-up, correlation,
batch evidence, restart and safe/finalized-head paths, not only live replay.

No signer cache is needed or trusted by a follower. A clean follower must derive
from the canonical anchor, available L1/DA inputs and chain configuration alone.

## 5. Incremental signer validation for long spans

Increasing the block ceiling alone would leave the whole ordinary history to be
re-executed inside a Sync deadline. Include incremental validation in this plan,
using the existing persistent per-block witness store as the producer-side source.
It changes internal proving work, not what cross-chain settlement authorizes.

### 5.1 Internal RPC extensions

Add backward-compatible methods to `prove.v1.Prover` and an additional Prove
chunk variant; retain existing message numbers and semantics:

- `Capabilities`: supported operations/profile versions, activation timestamp,
  maximum total window blocks, request bytes/witness items, preparation chunk
  ceiling, effective per-message limit, timeout values, and validation identity.
  The identity binds rollup ID, EIP-155 chain ID, chain/fork configuration digest,
  expected system address and a validator-schema/revision identifier. It does not
  expose private keys.
- `PrepareOrdinary(stream ...)`: complete ordinary block RLP/witnesses, in bounded
  chunks, with expected common environment and parent linkage. It performs actual
  Stateless validation and the §4.1 recipe equivalence checks. Return only the
  verified block hashes and the current cache generation; **never a settlement
  signature or a safe-head claim**.
- `CachedOrdinaryBlock` Prove chunk: number, block hash, parent hash and cache
  generation. It resolves only to locally validated immutable facts. A hash or
  token supplied by the composer is not evidence by itself.

The final `Prove` request may mix cached ordinary references and fully witnessed
ordinary blocks, but the terminal is always fully witnessed and freshly checked.
Every logical block counts against the total window ceiling even if it uses a
reference. Unknown/evicted references return a structured retryable cache-miss
result with the missing block identity, not an actionable cross-chain failure.

Preparation uses a header-first stream: rollup ID, expected validation identity
and proposed common environment, followed by ascending `BlockWitness` values.
It requires a nonempty contiguous ordinary range, at most 64 blocks. Each block's
parent is authenticated by its witness or the preceding validated header; no
client-supplied state-root shortcut is accepted. A fully validated ordinary block
that needs the full-record path can be cached too, marked ineligible for derived
use under that environment. Preparation failures return no reference for a failed
block; successfully validated immutable earlier facts may remain cached and can
be discovered/reused on retry. No partly validated entry is ever published.

Capability calls do not acquire the expensive execution permit. Preparation
streams have bounded ingestion queues and may not hold that permit while waiting
for more network input. Admission of a final proof preempts preparation between
block executions; one already-running block may finish, which is included in the
deadline tests. Retain the existing single active final-proof admission behavior.

Use `UNAVAILABLE` with a new structured cache-miss detail for missing references;
include generation and first missing block identity. The remote client invalidates
those references and schedules bounded preparation. It does not turn a cache miss
into eviction of a cross-chain source or repeatedly send the same unresolved
reference through `prove_with_retry`. If repair cannot fit the current target,
follow the existing unsent/failed-attempt reconciliation rules and keep ownership.
Malformed references and mismatched block identities are validation errors, not
cache misses that can be repaired by guessing another block.

Capabilities are advisory for resource planning, not cryptographic authority.
The existing returned-signature/public-input verification remains authoritative.
Recheck capabilities at connection/reconnection. A v3-enabled composer requires a
compatible signer; it must not guess limits when the endpoint is unavailable.
Legacy operation can use an old signer only with v3 emission disabled and an
explicitly compatible existing configuration.

### 5.2 Cache identity and integrity

Key cached facts by full block hash and validation identity. Store canonical block
RLP, authenticated parent/header facts, pre/post-state commitments, ordinary
system-sender classification and the verified derivation inputs. Different recipe
inputs must be checked against those exact facts; a validation for one environment
does not authorize another. Never key validity by height alone.

On final proof, verify the exact linked sequence, pre/post-state telescoping,
recipe match, requested terminal parent and all existing settlement binding.
Cached blocks can belong to another fork; their hashes are reusable facts, but
their place in this request is checked anew. Cached validation never marks data
canonical or settled.

Use a volatile byte-accounted cache with default ceilings **131,072 entries and
512 MiB of retained data/accounted metadata**, whichever is reached first. Include
an allowance for map/node overhead in accounting and separately measure process
RSS. Pin entries only while admitting/validating an active request. Evict unpinned
LRU entries; if space cannot be obtained, reject preparation before allocation.
Do not evict a referenced block halfway through an admitted proof.

A fresh process has a new cache generation. Restart invalidates references and
triggers bounded re-preparation from the existing durable witness store. A chain
configuration or validator revision change invalidates the whole namespace.
Cache loss is a performance event, not permission to sign unchecked data.

### 5.3 Scheduling, cancellation and storage

Prepare after a committed ordinary block's witness is durable. Default preparation
chunks contain at most **64 blocks**, additionally bounded by current byte/item
quotas; adapt to fewer blocks when needed. A single oversized block is reported
explicitly. Keep the preparation queue bounded and deduplicate by block hash.

Set the producer's preparation queue to at most 128 block identities; on overload
keep a canonical catch-up watermark instead of accumulating witnesses in RAM.
After catching up, verify the watermark's hash and rewind it to matching ancestry
after reorgs. Preparation drains from the existing durable witness store. A
separate lightweight reference index may span the bounded pending history, but
must not retain a second witness copy.

Use one shared validation worker/permit as today. Final proof requests have
priority at block boundaries; ordinary preparation checks cancellation between
blocks and cannot indefinitely starve a terminal proof. Streaming ingestion and
cache admission are also quota-bound. Timeout/cancellation must release permits,
pins and buffers; signing after deadline/cancellation remains forbidden.

Before selecting cross-chain work for an exact slot, require the ordinary prefix
to be prepared or demonstrably cold-validatable within the remaining budget.
Otherwise prewarm and use the existing readiness deferral; never move already
selected cross-chain effects to a different target or relax submission slack.
Keep owned sources queued. An anchor-only candidate may use the existing eligible
future-target selection after preparation; it is still bound to the final target
when signing.

Change composer witness assembly and `RemoteProver::chunks_for` to use lightweight
references for prepared ordinary blocks and move/stream full witnesses for cache
misses and the terminal. Do not build duplicate full-window witness vectors.
Retain witnesses durably until the existing L1-finalized purge floor. Verify
hashes on store hits, including after reorgs, exactly as the current witness source
does. Disk-full/missing-witness conditions fail closed and must not silently prune
unsettled history. The existing MDBX map ceiling is not a free-disk guarantee.

## 6. Encoding and resource accounting in the composer

Implement `DerivablePayloadSizer` beside the codec. The same shape definitions
must drive exact encoding and sizing; no empirical compression ratios are allowed.
It accounts for common environment, count/list prefixes, sparse record gaps,
transactions, full exceptions, unchanged terminal/entries/groups, and native
message framing/semantics.

Replace the old full-block item prefix accounting for v3. The activity index needs
a composable range summary containing block count, first/last record positions,
encoded record data lengths, gap-prefix lengths, and transaction activity. On
re-anchoring adjust the first record's gap; when a historical endpoint becomes
the terminal remove its ordinary representation and add its unchanged full
terminal representation. Simply subtracting old encoded-byte prefix sums is wrong.
Index/cache identity includes format, profile, environment digest and anchor/hash.
Reorgs rewind to matching ancestry; configuration changes invalidate summaries.

Use exact completed-record sizes and conservative bounds for unknown future
inputs. Derived ordinary blocks no longer reserve unknown output-root/bloom bytes.
Full exceptions and the future terminal still use full-block bounds. Account for
integer/list-prefix growth and worst-case explicit exception records before
admitting a transaction. Check the actual final encoding before committing a
newly built block/candidate; retain overflow transactions and nonce dependencies.
Keep active/future-fork blob maxima and companion consumption checks.

Update both ordinary pool admission/interval guards and final candidate sizing.
Preserve legal empty Sync boundaries used to split retained history. Include
logical block ceilings, signer capabilities and exact request-resource estimates
in feasible-prefix selection. A pending prefix must have a legal endpoint before
any applicable hard limit; reserve through that boundary. If no single legal
interval fits, reject startup/admission with a specific error rather than accepting
history that cannot settle. Existing incompatible retained history must be kept
and reported, never truncated.

Local resource failure may split ordinary history only at existing legal boundaries
and cannot split a cross-chain group. Missing/stale capability data pauses dependent
admission until refreshed. A lowered signer limit is detected before dispatch;
already accepted history drains through feasible historical prefixes where possible.

## 7. Defaults and the meaning of “large enough”

| Limit | Planned default / behavior |
|---|---|
| Signer total blocks per request | **65,536**, replacing 512; operator override retained. |
| V3 format maximum total blocks | **65,536**, enforced by every decoder, independent of local operational caps. |
| Aggregate Prove/Prepare request bytes | Existing **512 MiB**; references are charged by their encoded request size, cached data remains bounded separately. |
| Aggregate streamed witness-array items | Existing **1,000,000** per request; every cold block is validated, across as many bounded preparations as required. |
| Effective server message maximum | Existing **256 MiB**, or a smaller request limit; client honors the advertised maximum instead of assuming its current 1 GiB setting is accepted. |
| Stream idle / total request deadline | Existing **120 / 600 seconds**; target-slot deadline takes precedence for final posting. |
| Preparation chunk | At most **64 blocks**, further reduced by byte/item limits. |
| Validation concurrency | One worker, terminal priority between blocks; no concurrent unbounded warmup. |
| Signer cached facts | At most **131,072 entries / 512 MiB accounted memory**. |

These are implementation decisions. Validation must show they meet the targeted
empty/light-history workloads. If the acceptance workload cannot be prepared or
proved under these limits, the release gate fails: fix the implementation or amend
the explicit, reviewed resource envelope and rerun tests. Do not quietly claim
65,536 usable blocks after testing only header admission.

Signer reference resolution remains bounded by the same total-block maximum;
preparing blocks in several calls must not bypass the final request's count cap.
On-chain follower acceptance uses format/consensus limits, not another operator's
RPC/cache settings. A follower with insufficient local resources reports inability
to sync, not a different validity rule for an otherwise valid batch.

Existing ordinary time/count posting triggers and speculative-depth configuration
remain effective. Document configurations that allow the intended multi-hour
history and validate their consistency with the signer and legal grid. Do not
silently increase latency settings or disable cross-chain due rules.

## 8. Activation, history and rollback

Add one coordinated setting, `EEZ_CHAIN_OPERATION_V3_ACTIVATION_TIMESTAMP`, an
unsigned L2 Unix timestamp. Absence disables v3 acceptance/emission. Persist it
with the deployment's reviewed chain/runtime configuration and expose it in signer
capabilities. All readers/signers/writers must agree before activation. This is a
proposed setting to implement, not an existing supported option.

V3 eligibility is decided by the timestamp of its retained full terminal header,
which the signer validates and the follower binds through the existing settlement
path. Earlier ordinary history may cross the activation timestamp because every
ordinary position explicitly selects a supported derivation or full-block path.
Reject v3 with a terminal before activation. Keep old formats valid afterward so
historical replay and writer rollback remain possible. Never reinterpret old data.

Rollout order: shared codec/replay support and tests; readers and signer; capability
and configuration checks; writer activation at the selected future timestamp.
Run a clean follower through pre/post-activation history before declaring success.
Deployment commands are a later operational task, not part of this plan execution.

Rollback disables new writer emission while retaining v3 readers. Restore a
previous writer only if it includes v3 historical decoding and can drain retained
history using legal legacy-sized prefixes. Never roll a reader back to a binary
unable to read already settled v3 data. Retain witness storage, checkpoints and
canonical history; no chain reset or data rewrite.

## 9. Work packages and ownership by component

| Order | Components | Deliverable / dependency |
|---|---|---|
| A | `eez-payload-codec`; proposal/golden fixtures | Exact v3 types, parser, encoder, iterator, size algebra and bounded decode; legacy fixtures unchanged. |
| B | `eez-driver::derivation`; pinned Reth adapter; `eez-proof-signer/validate/stateless.rs` | Shared execution inputs and ordinary full-block reconstruction from validated outputs. Depends on A. |
| C | `eez-deriver` live/catch-up/reconciliation/correlation; `eez-l1` evidence/example tools | New block plans throughout follower and tooling; preserve terminal and L1-applied endpoint gates. Depends on B. |
| D | `eez-proof-signer/settlement/da.rs`, service/limits/config; `SPEC.md` | V3 recipe-to-window checks, terminal binding unchanged, 65,536 default, bounded count/resource failures. Depends on B. |
| E | `eez-control-rpc/proto/prove.proto`, generated modules; `eez-prover`, `eez-prover-client`, signer service/cache | Capabilities, PrepareOrdinary, cached references, quota/cancellation/priority behavior. Depends on D. |
| F | `eez-node` proving/witness integration; composer proof-context construction | Durable-witness-triggered preparation, bounded retry/restart/reorg behavior, eliminate duplicate witness-window allocations. Depends on E. |
| G | `eez-composer` policy/index/sequencing/admission/encoding; `eez-node-common` payload/pool sizing | Exact v3 estimates, terminal promotion, feasible prefixes, capability checks and overflow prevention. Depends on A, E, F. |
| H | Composer/signer/follower launch configuration and deployment templates | Shared activation setting, compatibility checks, rollout and rollback instructions. Depends on C–G. |
| I | `eez-node-e2e`, signer integration tests, CI and research artifacts | Complete equivalence/adversarial/performance evidence and operator capacity envelope. Release depends on all gates. |

Review in these bounded packages; no package may silently change the wire shape or
shared defaults. A discovered omission updates this specification and its coverage
row before implementation proceeds. Production activation remains disabled until
package I passes.

The initial requirement-to-component mapping is in the
[coverage ledger](derivable-chain-operations-coverage.md). Every entry starts as
planned; implementation must replace that status with code and evidence links.

## 10. Correctness and failure coverage

| Area | Required cases and assertions |
|---|---|
| Codec | Empty ordinary range; one/65,535 ordinary blocks; reject 65,536 ordinary blocks; RLP prefix boundaries; malformed/truncated/overflow inputs; unknown tags/profile/kind; gaps past end; extra records; wrong terminal count; signed transaction byte identity. |
| Scope preservation | Compare encoded terminal, entries, group sizes and outer semantic suffix byte-for-byte before/after. Verify the same physical packing rules and public-input/KZG binding. |
| Derived execution | Empty/nonempty/reverted blocks; legacy/2930/1559/7702 and every other currently accepted transaction type; block boundaries and ordering; zero and changed environment; fallback before/after derived blocks; contract reads of NUMBER/TIMESTAMP/COINBASE/PREVRANDAO/GASLIMIT/BASEFEE/BLOCKHASH; pre/post-execution system transitions. |
| Forks | All currently supported post-Merge L2 configurations, first Shanghai/Cancun/Prague/Osaka blocks where applicable, supported boundary crossing, optional field presence, future unsupported profile transition uses full records or rejects. |
| Signer tampering | Valid txs with altered environment/count/gap; header outputs differing from assembly; wrong parent/config; system sender hidden as ordinary; missing transactions; wrong terminal/entry binding; no attestation on any mismatch. |
| Settlement | Full, partial, deferred, reverted, resumed and competing same-L1-block paths; canonical applied-prefix endpoint, outbound event gate and value effects unchanged. Include terminal-only and fallback ranges. |
| Cache trust | Wrong block/height/parent/environment/generation/config; stale fork, eviction before/after pinning, corrupt/missing entries, reused reference in incompatible window; cold and cached results identical. Cache cannot authorize system transactions or terminal observations. |
| Resources | Every quota boundary; count checked before expansion; Prepare chunks cannot evade final count; cache accounting includes overhead; cancellation/timeout releases memory/permits; cold validation and preparation cannot starve final proof. |
| Persistence/reorg | Node/signer restarts with pruned parent state; rebuild from durable witnesses; witness hash mismatch; no purge above finalized floor; L1 rollback and alternate L2 ancestry; reader catch-up without producer RPC. |
| Sizing | Encoded size equals estimate for completed candidates; conservative future reservation; new first gap on re-anchor; ordinary-to-terminal promotion; historical splits; all RLP thresholds; next-nonce preservation and individually unpostable transactions. |
| Operational limits | Lower signer/operator limits, capability unavailability/reconnect/change, stale target slot, missing witness, disk/cache full; retain owned sources and accepted history with explicit bounded recovery. |
| Compatibility | Old tags/old fixtures; old signer with v3 disabled; incompatible signer prevents v3 launch; before/at/after activation; retained-v3 writer rollback; clean follower through mixed formats. |

Run affected unit/integration tests, the existing native settlement/cross-chain
suite on Ethereum and Gnosis profiles, all-target Clippy, formatting and whitespace
checks. Unit round trips do not substitute for independent follower execution.
Use property tests for record/gap size composition and parser bounds and fuzz the
new parser/iterator, including maximal declared runs with minimal input.

## 11. Performance gates and evidence

Use fixed chain configuration and immutable transaction inputs. Compare old full
blocks, the new recipe with cold proof validation, and the prepared-reference path.
Measure physical blob counts from actual final encodings, not corpus-wide sums.

Required span sizes: **512, 1,024, 4,096, 10,000, 43,200 and 65,536 total blocks**.
For each, exercise empty history and a sparse deterministic transfer workload that
fits the same six-blob example allowance; also run boundary-filling and high-entropy
data workloads whose expected result may be a smaller feasible prefix. Do not
claim every workload should fit 65,536 blocks. Account for the unchanged terminal
and semantic bytes explicitly.

Required measurable outcomes:

1. A 43,200-block empty-history candidate and a 65,536-block empty-history
   candidate encode within the actual allowed blob count, with no per-empty-block
   header bytes. They independently replay to exact original block hashes.
2. The signer accepts the fully valid largest-window example with the planned
   defaults using bounded preparation, and rejects 65,537 total blocks. The
   terminal still receives full fresh validation.
3. Prepared-path final proof plus remaining preparation fits the configured
   submission deadline for both native L1 profiles in the test environment; record
   at least 20 warm repetitions, median/p95/max and misses. All repetitions must
   fit the release profile's deadline; no fixed hardware-independent seconds are
   invented in this plan. Cold recovery times are reported separately.
4. Existing cross-chain latency/deadline tests remain passing under concurrent
   background preparation. No group changes target, order or semantic bytes to
   achieve the timing result.
5. Record peak composer/signer/follower RSS, cache-accounted bytes, witness DB
   growth, request bytes/items, disk reads and cache hit/miss rates. Cache and
   request quotas must hold under adversarial and cancellation cases; the report
   specifies the minimum tested machine resources and configuration.
6. Steady-state block accounting/preparation processes new work incrementally;
   no full-history rescans each L2 tick or full witness copies at each proof retry.
   Document catch-up/reorg costs separately.

Emit structured measurements keyed by anchor hash, candidate terminal hash and,
after dispatch, postBatch hash. Include payload/profile versions, ordinary total,
derived-empty/nonempty/full-exception counts, unchanged terminal/entry/semantic
bytes, encoded stream bytes, actual blobs, cache hit/miss counts, witness request
bytes/items, preparation/proof/replay times, and the precise limiting constraint.
Do not count retries as additional settled capacity. Never log witness contents,
private keys or full user transaction data merely to measure their lengths.

If any required gate fails, the implementation is not complete. Resolve the
failure without reducing scope, weakening verification, dropping cross-chain tests
or silently lowering the claimed supported empty-history span. Any proposed
resource/default or architecture amendment is recorded and revalidated explicitly.

Artifacts include repository/dependency/binary identities, activation/configuration,
input hashes, per-block replay comparisons, receipt/commitment checks, byte tables,
timing/memory logs and exact reproduction commands. The final operator guide
separates the 65,536 format/default ceiling from measured transaction-volume and
hardware-dependent capacity.

## 12. Definition of done

- Every normative rule above has an implementation and test/evidence link in a
  checked-in coverage ledger; no unassigned design questions or missing rows.
- New on-chain data differs only within `ChainOperation.operations` and consequent
  carrier lengths/commitments. All original blocks and cross-chain results agree.
- Full history is derivable by an independent follower from authenticated inputs;
  no local signer cache or sequencer header service becomes a DA dependency.
- Signer defaults, preparation, admission and posting deadlines support the tested
  long-empty-history spans without relocating cross-chain effects or accepting
  unbounded work.
- Backward compatibility, partial settlement, reorg, restart, activation and writer
  rollback are verified; no live deployment is implied by finishing the code.

This plan removes unowned implementation decisions. It does not assert that
untested code has no defects; the release gates are how the remaining empirical
questions are resolved before the change is considered complete.
